newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Deal near for Swedish S-E-Banken, Nordbanken-paper.
newsitem.headline: Deal near for Swedish S-E-Banken, Nordbanken-paper.

text.p: Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken are close to reaching a comprehensive cooperation agreement, Swedish business daily Dagens Industri said on Saturday.

Nordbanken will take over S-E-Banken's nationwide network of bank offices and Nordbanken will sell its international division and mutual fund operation to S-E-Banken to become a merchant bank, the newspaper said, citing unnamed sources.
The deal will result in the elimination of some 3,000 or more jobs in the two banks, the newspaper said.
The banks will announce the deal within a month, or, at the latest, this autumn, it said. Both the banks had also considered deals with foreign banks, the newspaper said.

A merger between the two had been flagged by financial markets for many months. Talks resumed in the spring after the two banks announced in February that they had abandoned negotiations, the newspaper said.

"The talks got a new impetus after April 29, when Jacob Wallenberg was appointed as the new chief executive of S-E-Banken. Former S-E-Banken CEO Bjorn Svedberg had reportedly opposed splitting up the bank," Dagens Industri said.

Sweden's Wallenberg family has been increasing control of S-E-Banken throughout late 1996 and early 1997 so that it now controls over 20 percent of votes in S-E-Banken, in part through Swedish investment group Investor, it said.
The expected restructuring means the state can sell most of its 59.4 percent stake in Nordbanken which is estimated to bring some 26 billion crowns to state coffers, the newspaper said.
